question.text: If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mfenced><mi>x</mi></mfenced></math> is the solution of the differential equation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mfenced><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>y</mi></mrow></mfenced><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>y</mi><mfenced><mn>1</mn></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, and the slope of the curve <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi><mfenced><mi>x</mi></mfenced></math> is never zero, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mi>y</mi><mfenced><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mfenced></math> is _____ .

solution.text:
Given differential equation is dyy2-4y=dxx

⇒141y-4-1ydy=dxx

Integrating both sides, we get, 

14lny-4y=lnx+c

Given, y1=2

i.e. c=0

So, y-4y=±x4 or, y=41±x4

Considering y=41+x4

So, 10y2=1041+4=8
